insights: Tasks accepted before their promised service windows begin are considerably more prone to being completed too early.
Pickup tasks with longer promised service windows exhibit substantially higher compliance than tasks constrained by narrower windows.
Pickup duration does not increase uniformly with travel distance; instead, tasks exhibit distinct duration patterns across different distance ranges.
summary: Pickup completion in this multi-courier sample depends on both timing and task constraints. Tasks accepted before their windows are disproportionately completed early, wider promised windows have higher compliance, and travel distance produces distinct duration regimes rather than a simple increasing relationship.
